test.name: When macOS 27 cleans the user temporary folder that holds the daemon runtime root

expected: observing a reboot and a multi day idle period on macOS 27 shows when the contents of confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR) are removed, and a running stacklyd recreates its runtime root and socket at the next socket check
reason: the observation needs a reboot of this Mac and a multi day idle period with the runtime root left in place, which the user's policy records as heavy manual steps; the daemon side is covered: removing the socket and the runtime root while stacklyd runs brings both back at the next socket check (apps/daemon/tests/server/lifecycle.rs, a_socket_and_runtime_root_removed_while_serving_come_back_at_the_next_check), and the daemon lock lives in the data root, not in the temporary folder (spec 0004)
owner: ojiepermana (the user): run the steps below across a reboot and a few idle days, then record the result in spec 0004 (Follow-up for feature 6) through /architect and in a new record
steps: run `getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR` and start `stacklyd`; note the runtime root `<temp>/stackly` and its socket
stop stacklyd, leave `<temp>/stackly` in place with a marker file, and reboot this Mac; after login check whether the folder and the marker are still there
leave a second marker untouched for at least 4 days without a reboot and check again, since macOS removes old files in the user temporary folder after a few days
with stacklyd running, wait for the next cleanup and check the daemon log for `socket_rebound` and that `stackly daemon status` still works
write the dates and findings into a new record and into the spec 0004 Follow-up
